cases.question: If an online store can't ship my order in the time it promised, what does federal law say it has to offer me?
cases.answer:
Federal law, specifically 16 CFR § 435.2, requires that if a seller is unable to ship merchandise within the time stated in the solicitation, the seller must offer the buyer, clearly and conspicuously and without prior demand, an option to either consent to a delay in shipping or to cancel the buyer's order and receive a prompt refund. This offer must be made within a reasonable time after the seller first becomes aware of the inability to ship, but no later than the original applicable time.

The law also specifies that the offer must fully inform the buyer of their right to cancel and obtain a prompt refund, and it must provide a definite revised shipping date, or inform the buyer that the seller cannot make any representation regarding the length of the delay.
